Marissa / team — attaching draft responses and the SOC 2 package we can share under NDA. Below are high-level callouts that map to the FFIEC sections; details are in the attached Redwood_Response_FFIEC_Answers.docx and the resilience diagram.

Governance & oversight:
- Redwood maintains an executive security council and quarterly risk review for production-facing inference services; documented in our security governance playbook.
- Change control: all model and runtime changes go through code review + canary rollouts; rollback policy enforced by runtime.

Third-party risk management:
- We maintain an approved vendor list and conduct annual security reviews for critical suppliers (cloud, KMS, observability).
- Subprocessors: list included in questionnaire (we redacted non-material PII).

Encryption & key management:
- Data at rest: AES-256. In transit: TLS 1.3. Customer data may be segmented by tenant and can be configured to use customer-managed keys (CMK) with KMS/HSM integrations.

Incident response & forensics:
- IR runbook with tiered escalation and SR/PG notification timelines. We capture detailed request/response logs, full request IDs, and KV cache events to support forensic reconstruction.

Business continuity & disaster recovery:
- Multi-region deployment with automatic failover for Hosted API; Dedicated and Private offer region/zone isolation per contract. RTO and RPO targets vary by deployment tier; default Dedicated SLA: 99.9% with documented runbooks and annual DR drills. See resilience_diagram.png for recovery topology.

Audit & logging:
- Retention configurable by customer; default 30 days with paid extensions. Immutable audit logs, tamper-evident storage, and export via secure S3 or syslog endpoints.

Evidence provided: Redwood_SOC2_report.pdf, resilience_diagram.png.

I also noted two FFIEC-specific asks in the spreadsheet: 1) proof of annual DR exercise frequency, 2) sample of a red-team incident report. We can provide an executive summary and sanitized incident report under NDA.

-Vivek
